item.title: Common Ground Book Club: books by & about people with disabilities — Fri Sep 4, 10:30 AM — Sebastopol Library
item.description:

Drop-ins are welcome. If you didn't have time to read or finish the month's book, you are still welcome to attend. Snacks will be provided. Common Ground Society serves families who have loved ones with any sort of unique need while also educating our community on how to be inclusive. Held the 1st Friday of the month from 10:30-11:30am. We will not be meeting in January. 12/05/2025- December's title is Unfit Parent : A Disabled Mother Challenges An Inaccessible World by Jessica Slice 2/06/2025- Disability Intimacy: Essays on Love, Care, and Desire: Edited by Alice Wong 3/06/2025- The Kiss Quotient by Helen Hoang 04/03/2025- True Biz by Sara Nović 05/01/2025- Second Life: Having a Child in the Digital Age by Amanda Hess

item.title: QPR (Question, Persuade, Refer) — Fri Sep 4, 1:00 PM — Student Health Services
item.description:
Learn how to recognize the warning signs of suicide, start a supportive conversation, and connect someone to help. QPR (Question, Persuade, Refer) is a suicide prevention training that gives you practical skills to recognize when someone may be struggling and take action. Whether you're interested in mental health, supporting friends and peers, or simply want to be better prepared to help someone in need, this training can help you feel more confident responding to a crisis. In this training, you'll learn how to:Recognize warning signs and risk factors Identify when someone may be experiencing a mental health crisis Ask about suicide in a direct and supportive way Connect someone with appropriate help and resources Use the QPR approach to support someone in need To register visit the Student Health Services website. (https://shs.santarosa.edu/9-4-26-qpr)
Source: Santa Rosa Junior College

item.title: UC Master Gardeners - Climate Adaptation in Your Garden — Sat Sep 5, 10:30 AM — Windsor Regional Library
item.description:
This talk offers concrete, achievable, science-based means to use your own garden for carbon sequestration, food security, plant and animal habitat, and increased resilience to extreme weather and other climate change events. Leah Halper is a Master Gardener and Garden Sense consultant who helps Sonoma County residents transition their yards to use less water and support more beneficial plants and animals. She is also a UCANR-trained Climate Steward with special interest in resilience food gardening, carbon sequestration, and preserving habitat for plant and animal species at risk. Registration Encouraged: Visit Upcoming Events to complete your registration. After registering, you will receive a confirmation email containing information about attending the library talk. Learn about home gardening, pest management, water conservation practices, and more from your Sonoma County UC Master Gardeners! Different presentation topic per location.

item.title: Arjun Verma - Northern Classical Indian Concert — Sat Sep 5, 2:00 PM — Windsor Regional Library
item.description:
Immerse yourself in Northern Indian Classical music featuring sitar and tabla. Arjun K. Verma is an Indian-American sitarist and composer. Beginning with his father, Roop Verma, and continuing with the legendary Ali Akbar Khan and his son Alam Khan, Arjun's meticulous training has imbued him with a rich musicality that encompasses both the profound majesty and the exhilaration of North Indian classical music. Hailed by the New York Times as a "fine sitarist," Arjun shares the jewels of his cultural heritage in a manner that is fresh, modern, and relevant, while maintaining a high standard of traditional integrity.

item.title: You are Invited to North Bay Speech Masters Toastmasters Club Meeting — Sun Sep 6, 10:30 AM — Cogir of the North Bay
item.description:
Whether it's improving our health, focusing on professional advancement, learning a new skill, it is often helpful to obtain someone to help learn new skills like speaking without preparation. The group at Toastmasters can help.
We call speaking without preparation, impromptu speaking. If you want to learn new Impromptu speaking skills, Toastmasters can help. During the meeting, we will practice our impromptu speaking skills during our session we call Table Topics. During the Table Topics, the speaker is given a question, and they are asked to speak for 60 seconds to 2 minutes about the question.
Outside Toastmasters, impromptu speaking happens constantly. You might recognize it in moments such as:
--Being asked for your opinion in a meeting
--Responding to a follow-up question during a presentation
--Introducing yourself or someone else unexpectedly
--Handling a difficult or unplanned question

item.title: Watercolor | Building Technique II, with Nancy Ballard — Tue Sep 8, 10:00 AM — Petaluma Arts Center
item.description:
Building on the skills and confidence you developed in the first class, this watercolor workshop invites you to take your ideas a step further. Explore how a simple sketch, thoughtful composition, and expressive use of color can transform an idea into a finished painting.
We'll work larger and bolder while exploring watercolor techniques including:
Wet-on-wet paintingLoose interpretation and expressive mark-makingCreating shadows and depthEnhancing backgroundsWorking in black and whiteExploring the many variations and possibilities of mixing greens
Bring a favorite photograph, a live flower or small plant, or even a meaningful memory to use as inspiration. No matter where you are in your artistic journey, you'll be encouraged to experiment, have fun, and focus on the larger picture rather than striving for perfection. There are no mistakes in art—only opportunities to explore.
Please Note: There will be a $10 supply fee paid directly to the Nancy on the day of the class.

item.description: Each month, the Poetry Book Club meets online to discuss one must-read book of poems, whether a timeless classic or an award-winning contemporary. Led by Napa poet Kathleen Patterson, who has been an enthusiastic book club member since its beginning, meetings are open to all levels of poetry readers, both the curious and the committed. item.title: Marin Farmers Markets — Thu Sep 10, 8:00 AM — Marin Veterans' Memorial Auditorium
item.description:
Price: Free
Sponsor: Marin Center
Explore the bounty of summer at the Marin Farmers Markets. Taste vine-ripened tomatoes, corn that was picked that morning, and peaches so juicy you have to bend over just to get a bite. Farm-fresh eggs, grass-fed beef, artisan c heeses, raw milk, and freshly baked breads complete the shopping exper ience. Specialty prepared foods and handmade art add to the magic of the market.
Enjoy the intimate feeling of the Thursday Marin Farmers Market, an ideal place to meet for lunch and pick up fresh produce for the weekend. Discover the abundance and diversity of product at the celebrated Sunday Marin Farmers Market, the third largest farmers market in California. Turn your dollar into a vote for local sustainable agriculture, shrink your eco-footprint, and revive the feeling of being intimate ly connected to your food by meeting your farmers face-to-face. The market takes place rain or shine.
www.aginstitutemarin.org
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Dem
